answer: Coordinated Action Pricing requires each agent identity to independently complete verifiable task pairs before gaining network access, ensuring the cost scales with genuine human coordination rather than token wealth. An operator cannot offload work onto duplicate accounts, since every identity on a shared terrace must perform its own distinct proof. Trying to fragment tasks across many fake profiles forces the attacker to pay for each sonnet-equivalent unit separately, and as attempts multiply the total expense rises like a receding tide they cannot stem.
